nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $k$ a natural number and $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1}$ natural numbers. The group $G$ has a subset factorization of type $(a_0, \dots, a_{k-1})$ when there are finite subsets $A_0, \dots, A_{k-1}$ of $G$ with $|A_i| = a_i$ for every $i$ such that $G = A_0 A_1 \cdots A_{k-1}$, that is, every $g \in G$ can be written as $g = x_0 x_1 \cdots x_{k-1}$ with $x_i \in A_i$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Factorization of a group into subsets of given sizes

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 3$ there are a finite group $G$ and natural numbers $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1}$, each at least $2$, with $a_0 a_1 \cdots a_{k-1} = |G|$, such that there are no subsets $A_0, \dots, A_{k-1}$ of $G$ with $|A_i| = a_i$ for every $i$ and $G = A_0 A_1 \cdots A_{k-1}$, that is, with every element of $G$ a product $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_{k-1}$ where $x_i \in A_i$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Finite groups without subset factorizations exist for every length

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $k \ge 3$ there are a finite group $G$ and natural numbers $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1}$, each at least $2$, with $a_0 a_1 \cdots a_{k-1} = |G|$, such that $G$ has no subset factorization of type $(a_0, \dots, a_{k-1})$: there are no subsets $A_0, \dots, A_{k-1}$ of $G$ with $|A_i| = a_i$ for every $i$ and $G = A_0 A_1 \cdots A_{k-1}$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.35: counterexamples to subset factorization of every length
